# Text S1. Detecting fault planes in seismicity

**Why planes, not clusters.** A first version found clusters by density (DBSCAN: eight neighbors within
2.5 km in 3D). It kept only the densest knots (20% of events) and missed long, sparse alignments such as
the plate boundaries, because density never tests whether events lie on a plane. The method used here
searches for planes directly, in the spirit of anisotropic clustering [@Ouillon2008; @Wang2013] and of
recent hypocenter-based fault models [@Alongi2025].

**Detection.** (Code: `workflow/07_faults/fault_surfaces_planes.py`.)
- Events: at least four P and four S picks, catalog depth ≥ 0, Axial Seamount excluded (76,281 events).
- Tolerance: $\tau = 1.5\sqrt{(1.5\,|n_h|)^2 + (3\,n_z)^2}$ km for a plane with unit normal $n$ (about 2.3 km
  for a vertical plane, 4.5 km for a horizontal one).
- Seeds from dense to sparse; 150 random planes per seed through the seed and two events within 10 km,
  scored in a 20 km ball [@Fischler1981]; growth through events within $\tau$ that are connected in the
  plane (4 km cells, 8-connectivity); acceptance with ≥ 30 events, planarity $\sqrt{\lambda_3/\lambda_2} \le
  0.5$, in-plane width ≥ 1 km, dip ≥ 30° (v4 depths cannot resolve flatter structures; a diffuse cloud
  passes for a flat plane).
- Reassignment (three passes, k-planes): each event to the plane with the smallest $|d|/\tau$ whose
  rectangle contains its projection.
- Merging: normals within 15°, each within $\tau$ of the other, events closer than 4 km, joined set still
  planar.
- Rectangles: the 2–98% range of the events along strike and down dip plus 0.5 km; plane or quadratic by
  BIC; 1 km grid.

**Result.** 155 faults detected; 10 removed (Text S3); Blanco redone as strands (Text S2); 141 in the
product, 70% of events assigned (Table S1: `data/faults/v0/fault_surfaces_v0_assignment.csv`).
Fig. S1: map of events colored by fault (`fault_surfaces_v0_map.png`).

# Text S2. Uncertainty, stability and Blanco strands

**Uncertainty per vertex** (1σ normal to the surface): bootstrap of the fault's events (100 draws); Monte
Carlo moving each event by N(0; 1.5, 1.5, 3 km); spread over model choices (plane or quadratic, with or
without trimming beyond 2.5 RMS); combined in quadrature, median 0.44 km (10th–90th percentile 0.17–0.78
km). The catalog's `spatial_sigma` (3–20 km) is not used: events scatter only 0.6–1.8 km about the fitted
surfaces, so it behaves like an absolute, not a relative, error. Strike and dip intervals come from the
bootstrap; the full ensemble is provided (`fault_surfaces_v0_ensemble.csv.gz`).

**Stability.** Detection rerun with two other random seeds and tolerance factors 1.25 and 1.75; for each
fault, the median Jaccard overlap of its events with the best match; "stable" if ≥ 0.5 (50 of 141).
Overlap is low where parallel planes trade events between runs, even when the geometry barely moves.

**Blanco strands** (`workflow/07_faults/split_strands.py`, `merge_surfaces.py`). Strands are lines in map
view within 20° of plate motion (111°), 1.5 km half width, grown across gaps under 4 km, merged when
collinear. Two overlapping parallel strands stay separate only if Ashman's D > 2 [@Ashman1994] over the
overlap and within each year with ≥ 15 events in each. Depth test: the dip a single fault would need to
produce the offset. The literature check then removed six NW-trending strands in the Cascadia Depression
(where published faults strike N–S) and merged two depth-dependent "deeper band" strands. Table S2
(`fault_surfaces_v0_strand_separation.csv`) lists the 22 remaining pairs. Fig. S2: Blanco strands with
their events and top edges.

# Text S3. Removed surfaces

Six surfaces were quarry blasts (mostly daytime, weekday events: ON012, ON020, ON023, ON029, ON037, ON040),
four were artefacts (BL022, BL024, BL026: deep planes where published Blanco seismicity stops at 10–14 km;
PU010: a seismogenic-layer artefact), six were strand-search artefacts and two were merged
(`fault_surfaces_v0_removed.csv`, with reasons).

# Text S4. Comparison with the literature

Five searches, one per region (Blanco; Mendocino triple junction; Gorda; Puget and offshore Washington;
onshore, offshore Oregon and Endeavour), compared each fault's position, strike, dip, length and depth with
published faults, ridge and transform segments, seismic zones and earthquake sequences. Matches carry a
confidence (high to none) and a class (known structure, duplicate, seismicity layer, no known counterpart).
Every DOI was checked on Crossref or DataCite; where no structure is known, the references describe the
area so the claim can be checked. USGS moment tensors were used only to compare surfaces with known
earthquakes, never to build them. Table S4: `fault_surfaces_v0_literature.csv` and
`fault_surfaces_v0_literature.html`; regional notes in `data/faults/v0/literature/`.

# Text S5. Building the catalog

(Adapted from the catalog draft, `paper/main.qmd`, Data and Methods.)

**Data.** Continuous data from 2010 to 2016 were retrieved with ROVER into a day-file archive read through
an indexed client (pnwstore); the `NC` and `BK` networks were requested from the NCEDC FDSN service.
Picks of catalog v4 come from 696 stations of 24 networks (`7A`, `7D`, `BK`, `C8`, `CC`, `CN`, `GS`,
`NC`, `NV`, `OO`, `PB`, `TA`, `UO`, `UW`, `X4`, `X9`, `XD`, `XG`, `XU`, `YG`, `YH`, `YW`, `Z5`, `ZZ`),
among them the Cascadia Initiative ocean-bottom stations [@Stone2018] and the cabled stations of the
Ocean Observatories Initiative at Axial Seamount.

**Picking.** ELEP [@Yuan2023] combines five EQTransformer models [@Mousavi2020] distributed by
SeisBench [@Woollam2022] (original, ETHZ, INSTANCE, SCEDC, STEAD) by second-order semblance over 0.5 s,
on 60 s windows stepped by 30 s, after a 4–15 Hz band-pass; a pick is the semblance maximum of each
segment above 0.05. Two region passes (2011–2015, 123–127°W; 2010–2015, 122–129°W) produced the ver3
table (39.6 million picks). Three fills completed it: ver4 adds region-run station-days left out of ver3
(9.9 million picks); ver5 adds ocean-bottom station-days without picks, including the Axial cabled
stations (11.4 million); ver6 adds the land strip 122–123°W (12.7 million), for 73.6 million picks on
509,249 station-days. Every pick keeps its identifier across versions.

**Association and location.** GENIE [@McBrearty2023], trained for 38–51°N, 119–132°W on synthetic
events in a 3D model, associated the ver6 picks day by day on the stations available each day; events
with at least five stations were kept and located, then relocated with GraphDD [@McBrearty2025] on
catalog and cross-correlation differential times. Catalog v4 (I. McBrearty) has 172,340 events and
2,503,189 arrivals. Quality metrics are the numbers of P and S picks, stations, the azimuthal gap and the
RMS residual; the "QC" subset used for fault surfaces requires at least 4 P and 4 S picks.

**Magnitudes (Route A).** Wood–Anderson amplitudes are measured once per station-day for every pick, in
windows that grow with distance after association (P: up to 1 + 0.03r s, S: up to 2 + 0.06r s); 99.6% of
v4 arrivals have one. Station magnitudes with the Hutton–Boore distance term are inverted for event and
station terms (separate for each deployment epoch) within 150 km, anchored to 3,416 ComCat local
magnitudes (scatter 0.21), and replaced by regional moment magnitudes above M 4.5. 130,767 events have a
magnitude.

**Known data issues.** Ocean-bottom records carry ship noise, short-duration events, T-phases and high
microseism noise on the shelf [@Hilmo2020]; fragmented station-days produce picks at every data join
(1,846 station-days removed in ver6, 6,073 flagged in ver5); `NC` and `BK` picks are missing in 2016 and
parts of 2010–2011 (Text S7). Depth limitations: see below.

**Offshore location check.** On the Gorda Ridge, catalog epicenters fall on the axial valley, while ComCat
epicenters of the same events lie 10–20 km east.

Large events missed: 15 of 61 ComCat M ≥ 5 (2010–2016) have no catalog event within 30 s and 80 km,
including the 8 December 2016 Mw 6.6 on the Mendocino transform (10 at the northern edge, 3 offshore in
2016 without ocean-bottom stations, 1 in the 2016 northern California pick gap, 1 on the Blanco in 2011;
script in the figure notes). Event 172113 (14:51:18, 4 P and 1 S, near Mount St. Helens) is the Mw 6.6 mis-associated: its P picks
are the Pn arrivals at 708–797 km, within 2 s of iasp91, and should be flagged. We repicked the Mw 6.6, its
M 4.7 aftershock and the January 2016 Gorda pair on 30-minute windows of all stations within 4° (279 for
the Mw 6.6, 193 of them `NC`/`BK`) with the same ELEP ensemble, kept the picks near the predicted
arrivals from the ComCat origins, and located them with NonLinLoc in the 3D model of the relocation and
in iasp91. The picks are clean to 400 km (Mw 6.6: 146 P, 54 S), but every station is east of the events
(nearest 156 km, gap 255–310°): depths go to the bottom of every search range and epicenters move 7–41 km
west of ComCat. The three missing events are added with the ComCat hypocenter and magnitude and our
picks (branch `fix/m66-2016`, `data/catalog_v4/fixes/m66_2016/`). Depth limitations: 23.5% of events above
the surface with depths read below sea level, 16.2% below the local surface; 3D relocation in progress.

# Text S6. Clustering: validation and sensitivity

(Code: `workflow/06_analysis/v4_clusters_zbz.py`; report
`data/catalog_v4/clusters_zbz/catalog_v4_clusters_report.html`.)
- Mc per region and year (maximum curvature + 0.2); b by maximum likelihood per region; $d_f$ = 1.6
  (measured epicentral D2 0.8–1.4, run as a variant); epicentral distance floored at 0.5 km.
- Parent search over the whole catalog with a rupture-length cap; events below Mc or without magnitude
  attached afterwards to their nearest parent.
- Shuffled catalogs (times permuted in each region): bimodality index drops from 1.6–3.4 to 0.3–1.6; only
  3–17% of shuffled events pass the real threshold (34% at Axial, whose clustered share is an upper bound).
- Validation: the 2010 and 2014 Gorda, 2011 and 2014 Vancouver Island, 2012 Explorer and 2015 Mendocino
  fault zone earthquakes are mainshock–aftershock sequences; the 2015 Axial eruption is one swarm.
- Sensitivity: 84–99% of events keep their background or clustered label under $d_f$ 1.3/2.0/estimated,
  3D distance, Mc + 0.3 and yearly Mc; a conservative threshold raises background by 1–32 points.
- Limits: the per-region Mc keeps 27,555 events; Mc differs between regions (0.75–2.45); the swarm rule's
  magnitude gap (0.5) is close to the ML uncertainty (about 0.2).

# Text S7. Magnitude of completeness maps

(Code: `workflow/06_analysis/v4_mc_maps.py`; README in `data/catalog_v4/mc_maps/`.)
Magnitudes rounded to 0.1; every b fit needs ≥ 30 events above the cutoff. Methods: maximum curvature
+0.2; b-value stability with the Shi–Bolt test over a five-bin window [@Woessner2005; @Shi1982] (the fixed
0.03 tolerance of the AgentSeismo code almost never passes with 250 events); goodness of fit on cumulative
counts at 90% and 95% [@Wiemer2000]. Maximum curvature + 0.2 is the most conservative at 84% of nodes;
b-value stability averages 0.19 lower and the best estimate 0.14 lower. The QC-only catalog (≥ 4 P and ≥ 4
S) leaves Mc unchanged (median difference 0.0, interquartile range ±0.1). The per-region Mc of the
clustering is at or above all three methods everywhere except the Blanco b-value-stability value (2.5
against 2.45). At Axial the frequency–magnitude distribution has two slopes, so the pooled goodness-of-fit
value is unstable (σ 0.94); use maximum curvature (0.7) or the node values (0.4–1.0).
